sources.title: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 Concerning the Protection of Personal Data
sources.verifiedSection: Personal Data Protection Law — official UAE Government overview
sources.verifiedSummary: The official overview describes rules for personal-data processing, confidentiality, individual rights and cross-border transfers, with statutory exceptions and scope conditions.
sources.applicationNote: Potentially relevant IF real, identifiable student or staff data are processed and the applicable legal scope is met. Current demo uses fictional events and no personal data.
sources.verificationLimit: Overview only; no claim that every UAE institution or all education records are governed identically. Check full law, implementing rules and institutional context.

sources.title: UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
sources.verifiedSection: Policy Objectives — human judgement and AI oversight
sources.verifiedSummary: The UAE Charter recognizes the value of human judgment, oversight, governance and accountability in AI development and use.
sources.applicationNote: Supports a proposed human-in-the-loop review gate. It is a policy principle, not a directly evidenced CNC machine-start rule.
sources.verificationLimit: Do not present the Charter alone as a penal law or a certified laboratory SOP.

sources.title: UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031
sources.verifiedSummary: The UAE Cabinet approved an AI strategy addressing education, skills, research, data infrastructure, governance and AI adoption in priority sectors.
sources.applicationNote: National policy context for education-focused AI innovation; does not by itself establish local classroom or machine-guard requirements.
sources.verificationLimit: Strategic aims are not statutory CNC safety obligations.

sources.title: National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence
sources.verifiedSection: Official policy overview — governance and human oversight
sources.verifiedSummary: The official overview addresses AI/ML security governance, tailored safeguards, human oversight in critical decisions and resilience testing.
sources.applicationNote: Candidate source for securing AI-generated educational recommendations and reviewing critical scenarios.
sources.verificationLimit: Full policy controls, sector coverage, and whether this prototype is in scope require further review; no certified compliance claim.

sources.title: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
sources.verifiedSection: Core principles — safety, transparency, responsibility, human oversight
sources.verifiedSummary: UNESCO identifies safety, accountability, traceability, privacy and ultimate human oversight as central AI ethics principles.
sources.applicationNote: International ethics comparator for simulated safety incidents and education governance recommendations.
sources.verificationLimit: A UNESCO recommendation is not automatically binding on a particular university or CNC laboratory.

sources.title: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.issuer: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.verifiedSection: AI RMF Core — Govern, Map, Measure and Manage; MAP 3.5
sources.verifiedSummary: The voluntary framework structures risk practice into Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, including documenting human oversight processes.
sources.applicationNote: Design reference for structured incident logging, risk reasoning and supervised mitigation.
sources.verificationLimit: Voluntary US framework, not UAE law. NIST states updates are under development.

sources.title: ITU-T Y.3172 Architectural framework for machine learning in future networks including IMT-2020
sources.verifiedSummary: Y.3172 specifies machine-learning pipeline, management and orchestration components for future telecommunications networks.
sources.applicationNote: Contest-requested ARCHITECTURE ANALOGY: data collection, evidence indexing, scenario processing, human review and output traceability.
sources.verificationLimit: Telecom/ML architecture; not a CNC machine safety standard and no claim of formal Y.3172 conformity.

sources.title: AI Ready Analysis Towards a Standardized Readiness Framework Report 2.0
sources.verifiedSection: Framework analysis — 13 readiness dimensions and policy gaps
sources.verifiedSummary: ITU AI Readiness Report 2.0 discusses 13 readiness dimensions and the identification of implementation, standards and policy gaps.
sources.applicationNote: Reference for mapping readiness limitations in data availability, oversight, technical assurance and skills.
sources.verificationLimit: Mapping dimensions is qualitative and does not constitute a national AI readiness measurement or official rating.
